papers.title: HIV vaccines guide rare immune cells to make broadly neutralizing antibodies
papers.authors: Gnanakaran S, Derdeyn CA.

papers.title: TIF1γ regulates stability of regulatory T cells during inflammation
papers.authors: Contreras-Castillo E, Zambrano-Romero JD, Núñez-Martínez HN, Marcial-Medina MC, Orozco-Cordoba J, Ríos-Ramírez D, Muñoz-Paleta O, Pérez-Vázquez D, Sáenz-Cabezas AF, Guadalupe García-Patiño M, Ramos-Balderas JL, Tapia-Urzúa G, Tenorio-Hernández L, Guerrero G, Cano-Domínguez N, Delgado-Zaldívar D, Candelario-Martínez A, Martínez-Racine I, Licona-Limón I, Madera-Salcedo I, Rosetti F, Crispín JC, Noriega LG, Nava P, Pérez-López A, Maravillas-Montero JL, Recillas-Targa F, Valdés VJ, Macías-Silva M, Robles-Flores M, Furlan-Magaril M, Kaartinen V, Henao-Mejía J, Flavell R, Licona-Limón P.
papers.abstract: Regulatory T (T<sub>reg</sub>) cells are essential for controlling inflammation and maintaining tissue homeostasis. Transcriptional intermediary factor 1-γ (TIF1γ) has been implicated in noncanonical TGFβ-Smad signaling in hematopoietic stem cells, but its role in T<sub>reg</sub> cell function has not been explored. Here we show that TIF1γ-deficient T<sub>reg</sub> cells lose Foxp3 expression and
summary_bullets: TIF1γ is required to maintain Foxp3 expression and stability of regulatory T cells during inflammatory responses.
TIF1γ-deficient Tregs lose their suppressive identity and convert to pro-inflammatory effector cells.
TIF1γ regulates Treg function through noncanonical TGFβ signaling pathways independent of canonical Smad mechanisms.

papers.title: Loss of cellular RNA homeostasis contributes to MDA5 activation during virus infection
papers.authors: Sampaio NG, Davis T, Gearing LJ, Dias Junior AG, Chauveau L, Wray-McCann G, Odon V, Liudkovska V, McAllan AL, Cursi C, Mayer A, Ratnadiwakara M, Änkö ML, Cieśla M, Hertzog PJ, Rehwinkel J.
papers.abstract: MDA5 is an innate immune RNA sensor that senses infection with a range of viruses and other pathogens. MDA5's RNA agonists are not well defined. Here we used single-nucleotide resolution crosslinking and immunoprecipitation (iCLIP) to study its ligands. Of note, upon infection with SARS-CoV-2 or encephalomyocarditis virus, MDA5 bound overwhelmingly to cellular RNAs. Many binding sites were introni
summary_bullets: MDA5 predominantly binds cellular RNAs rather than viral RNAs during SARS-CoV-2 and encephalomyocarditis virus infection
Loss of RNA homeostasis, particularly accumulation of introns, drives MDA5 activation during viral infection
Cellular RNA dysregulation, not viral RNA recognition, may be the primary trigger for MDA5-mediated antiviral immunity

papers.title: A novel CAF population coordinates hyper-suppressive regulatory T cell recruitment and localization in lung cancer
papers.authors: Ringham OR, Rivera M, Loffredo LF, Ozsoy MA, Healy CM, Cheng MF, Jin Y, Chen N, de Los Santos-Alexis K, Azizi E, Saqi A, Buechler MB, Concepcion-Crisol CP, Arpaia N.
papers.abstract: Across many solid tumor types, cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are abundant and heterogeneous, with distinct subpopulations exerting immunomodulatory functions. Here we identify a novel population of immunomodulatory CAFs (imCAFs) in primary lung adenocarcinoma and pulmonary metastases, characterized by cell adhesion molecule L1-like (CHL1) expression and enriched in immune regulation and che
summary_bullets: imCAFs expressing CHL1 coordinate recruitment and localization of hyper-suppressive regulatory T cells in lung tumors
CAF heterogeneity includes distinct immunomodulatory subpopulation that drives immune evasion through T cell regulation
Novel imCAF population represents therapeutic target for restoring anti-tumor immunity in lung cancer

papers.title: Decoding mechanoregulation in immunological synapses using biomimetic artificial cells
papers.authors: Yu X, Mukwaya V, Yue M, Yang S, Li Q, Zhao W, Fan C, Wang L, Zhao Y, Yang H, Su J, Wang L, Dou H.
papers.abstract: Mechanical force-driven signaling has emerged as a key regulator of cell-cell interactions (CCIs), which can enhance immune cell function. However, current biochemical approaches for studying CCIs offer minimal direct control over cellular bulk phenotypes, while synthetic biomaterial systems fail to mimic the dynamic complexity of cells. Here we introduce kpiCells, a biomaterial-based platform tha
summary_bullets: kpiCells platform enables precise mechanical force control in immune cell interactions, bridging gap between biochemical assays and complex cellular systems.
Mechanical forces regulate immunological synapse formation and enhance immune cell signaling through controlled biomimetic artificial cell systems.
Biomaterial approach provides dynamic complexity of living cells while maintaining experimental control over mechanical parameters in cell-cell interactions.

papers.title: PA200 modulates immunoproteasome structure and activity
papers.authors: Živković D, Bosc-Rosati A, Dafun AS, Mourtada F, Grygier P, Yazgili AS, Jansma M, Rawski M, Czarna A, Bohn S, Zak KM, Santos Dias Mourão A, Reiling N, Zemke L, Guo K, Behr J, Burlet-Schiltz O, Popowicz GM, Marcoux J, Meiners S, Bousquet MP.
papers.abstract: The proteasome activator PA200 binds to the catalytic core of both standard proteasome (s20S) and the immunoproteasome (i20S); however, whether PA200 uses the same mechanisms to activate i20S remains unknown. In this work, the cryo-EM structures of singly- and doubly-capped i20S-PA200 complexes, combined with complementary in vitro biochemical assays, show that binding of the first PA200 induces a
summary_bullets: PA200 activator binds immunoproteasome differently than standard proteasome, inducing unique structural conformational changes
PA200 binding to immunoproteasome shows cooperative effects with distinct mechanisms between single and double capping
Cryo-EM structures reveal PA200 modulates immunoproteasome catalytic activity through immunosubunit-specific interactions

papers.title: The genesis of cutaneous neurogenic inflammation is a multi-step process requiring dendritic cell aggregation
papers.authors: Chen CS, Gillis JE, Cohen JA, Glathar AR, Chen Y, Weiss ES, McKendrick LM, Bacon CO, Smith CJ, Spencer NJ, Chiu IM, Davis BM, Sumpter TL, Cillo AR, Poholek AC, Kaplan DH.
papers.abstract: Cutaneous inflammation involving neuroimmune interactions can be initiated by both neurons and immune cells, making it complicated to parse the mechanisms of neurogenic inflammation. Optogenetic activation of Trpv1-expressing nociceptors drives type-17 inflammation in the absence of other inflammatory triggers. We found that two rounds of nociceptor activation were required for Il23a expression an
summary_bullets: Two sequential nociceptor activation rounds are required to trigger IL-23a expression and type-17 cutaneous inflammation
Dendritic cell aggregation is a critical multi-step process linking nociceptor activation to neurogenic inflammation
Optogenetics enables dissection of neuroimmune mechanisms by specifically activating TRPV1+ nociceptors independently of other triggers

papers.title: Coordinated transcriptional networks program organelle expansion and metabolic flows for high endothelial morphology and function
papers.authors: Bi Y, Brulois K, Ayesha A, Xiang M, Ballet R, Ocón B, Dinh T, Lazarus N, Kunte M, Ramos G, Lupu F, Lin JH, Butcher EC, Pan J.
papers.abstract: High endothelial cells (HECs) control lymphocyte homing for adaptive immunity. They are defined by plump morphology, reflecting endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and Golgi expansion, and are by display of sulfo-sialomucins of the peripheral node addressin (PNAd) critical for lymphocyte recruitment. How these features are linked was unclear. Here, we found that HEC genes for sulfoglycoprotein synthesis an
summary_bullets: Coordinated transcription networks in high endothelial cells link organelle expansion with sulfoglycoprotein synthesis for lymphocyte recruitment function.
ER and Golgi expansion in HECs supports production of PNAd sulfo-sialomucins essential for adaptive immune cell homing.
Metabolic reprogramming accompanies organellar growth to fuel the biosynthetic demands of specialized HEC morphology and immunological function.

papers.title: Stearoyl-CoA desaturases regulate intestinal stem and progenitor cell metabolism and function in response to nutrient abundance
papers.authors: Akkaya-Colak KB, Keller AR, Festing MH, Gupta K, Sledziona J, Adeniyi A, West O, Stevens P, Pietrzak M, Knoblaugh SE, Walesewicz H, Baldwin DA, Denko NC, Simcox JA, Ntambi JM, Clinton SK, Mihaylova MM.
papers.abstract: Diet composition and nutrient availability play critical roles in intestinal stem and progenitor cell function and proliferation. Here, we show that stearoyl-CoA desaturases (SCDs) are regulated by nutrient abundance and link intracellular lipid metabolism to intestinal homeostasis. Pharmacological inhibition or genetic deletion of Scd1 and Scd2 in intestinal mouse organoids disrupted lipid desatu
summary_bullets: SCDs regulate intestinal stem/progenitor metabolism and are nutrient-responsive regulators of intestinal homeostasis.
SCD1/SCD2 inhibition disrupts lipid desaturation and impairs intestinal stem cell function and proliferation.
Intracellular lipid metabolism links nutrient availability to intestinal epithelial maintenance and regeneration.

papers.title: How and when to use artificial intelligence in your science job application
papers.authors: Payne D.

papers.title: Prevalence and chronology of colibactin-associated mutational processes and their microbiome spectra in Japanese colorectal cancer
papers.authors: Shiba S, Yachida S, Mizutani S, Totoki Y, Nakamura H, Hama N, Miyoshi N, Arai Y, Saito-Adachi M, Kimura H, Hayashi Y, Takamaru H, Tanaka K, Hayashi R, Rokutan H, Ikuta S, Kanemitsu Y, Doki Y, Eguchi H, Hattori S, Saito Y, Yamada T, Shibata T.
papers.abstract: The incidence of colorectal cancer (CRC) has risen in recent decades, with a disproportionate increase observed among younger individuals in Japan and other countries. The etiological contribution of the gut microbiota to CRC pathogenesis is recognized, yet the mechanisms involved remain to be fully clarified. Here we integrated whole-genome sequencing (WGS) and transcriptome profiling of CRC with
summary_bullets: Colibactin-producing bacteria generate distinctive mutational signatures in Japanese CRC tumors, with specific microbiome profiles associated with this genotoxic pathway.
Chronological analysis reveals colibactin-induced mutations occur early in CRC development, suggesting microbiota-driven carcinogenesis mechanisms precede malignant transformation.
Integration of genomics and transcriptomics identifies gut bacterial taxa linked to colibactin activity, providing mechanistic insights into microbiota-driven CRC pathogenesis.

papers.title: Mega-enhancers compartmentalize transcriptionally active long genes in the brain
papers.authors: Zhao Z, Payán Parra OA, Fujita SI, Musella F, Scrutton Alvarado NJ, Alber F, Yang Y, Yamada T.
papers.abstract: Exceptionally long genes and cis-regulatory enhancers are selectively activated in mammalian brain neurons, and these loci are mutation hotspots in neurological disorders. However, the organization of these large genomic elements at the level of chromosome folding, beyond local enhancer-promoter interactions, remains poorly understood. Here we report the discovery of a genomic subcompartment in th
summary_bullets: Mega-enhancers form distinct chromatin compartments that organize exceptionally long genes active in brain neurons
This compartmentalization architecture is disrupted in neurological disorder mutations, suggesting mechanistic links to disease
Long genes and their regulatory elements require specialized 3D genome organization for proper transcriptional control in the brain

papers.title: Author Correction: Regulatory T cells function in established systemic inflammation and reverse fatal autoimmunity
papers.authors: Hu W, Wang ZM, Feng Y, Schizas M, Hoyos BE, van der Veeken J, Verter JG, Bou-Puerto R, Rudensky AY.

papers.title: Latent effector T cells mediate immunotherapy responses in the bone marrow microenvironment
papers.authors: Kehl N, Wagner TR, Steiger S, Boschert T, Kilian M, Schach A, Michel JJ, Foster K, Hernandez GM, Ctortecka C, Metzler AD, Kirschner A, Van der Vreken A, Humer D, Onken R, Cuntz S, Zoller J, Funk C, Neunhäuser S, Mönnig M, Schönfelder B, Renders S, Maldonado Torres C, Sester LS, Frenking JH, Werner F, Osen W, Lindner K, Sen E, Schumacher S, Galas-Filipowicz D, Fitzsimons E, Green EW, Schmidt P, Lindner JM, Uhrig S, Bunse L, Chain B, Goldschmidt H, Weinhold N, Fröhling S, Sauer T, Raffel S, Abelin JG, Carr SA, Yong K, Trumpp A, Müller-Tidow C, Rippe K, Raab MS, Platten M, Eichmüller SB, Friedrich MJ.
papers.abstract: T cell-mediated immune surveillance is critical for cancer control, yet its role in bone marrow malignancies remains poorly understood. Here, we integrate TCR profiling, HLA immunopeptidomics, and functional screening to characterize tumor-reactive T cells in the bone marrow of patients with multiple myeloma (MM) and acute myeloid leukemia (AML). These cells are transcriptionally defined by a cons
summary_bullets: Tumor-reactive T cells in bone marrow malignancies display latent effector phenotype with capacity for immunotherapy response
TCR profiling and HLA immunopeptidomics identify patient-specific tumor-reactive clones in MM and AML bone marrow microenvironments
Functional characterization reveals bone marrow T cells can be activated for enhanced anti-tumor immunity through therapeutic intervention

papers.title: Functional and structural basis of Omicron BA.3.2.1 spike
papers.authors: Wang Y, Hu Y, Chen Z, Zou J, Zhang K, Ren P, Shi PY, Liang B, Xie X.
papers.abstract: SARS-CoV-2 BA.3.2 sublineages, derived from BA.3 and carrying substantial spike divergence, raised concerns about altered fitness and antigenicity. Using BA.3.2.1 as a representative strain, we engineered live-attenuated SARS-CoV-2 encoding BA.3.2.1, LP.8.1, or XEC spikes and benchmarked them against BA.3 and KP.3. BA.3.2.1 outcompetes BA.3 in primary human airway epithelium but replicates less ef
summary_bullets: BA.3.2.1 spike shows enhanced competitive fitness over BA.3 in human airway epithelium despite reduced overall replication efficiency.
Substantial spike sequence divergence in BA.3.2 sublineages alters viral properties while maintaining viable replication capacity.
Live-attenuated virus platform enables functional characterization of spike variants across contemporary SARS-CoV-2 lineages.

papers.title: PKR engages viral RNA and intron-retained host transcripts during poxvirus infection
papers.authors: Zhang R, Ye X, Dixson AC, Zhao Y, Weaver AM, Karijolich J.
papers.abstract: Recognition of double-stranded (ds) RNA is central to antiviral defense, yet how RNA sensors are activated during infection remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate that during vaccinia virus (VacV) infection, PKR binding is enriched on viral RNAs and host-intron-containing transcripts. During infection, RNase L activation impaired pre-mRNA splicing, promoting accumulation of cytoplasmic intron-retai
summary_bullets: PKR binds viral RNA and intron-retained host transcripts during vaccinia virus infection, revealing dual RNA targets for antiviral sensing.
RNase L activation during infection impairs pre-mRNA splicing, causing cytoplasmic accumulation of unspliced transcripts as PKR substrates.
Intron-containing transcripts become PKR ligands during poxvirus infection through disrupted splicing machinery, linking RNA processing to innate immunity.

papers.title: VOICE: A Vision-Omics Foundation Model Integrating Direct and Retrieval-Based Prediction of In-situ Single-Cell Gene Expression
papers.authors: Xin Luo, Yicheng Tao, Haoxuan Zeng, Suyuan Wang, Chenzi Ouyang, Meiqi Zhu, Kai Liu, Shuibing Chen, Jie Liu
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics can resolve gene expression at single-cell resolution, but it is costly, limited to targeted panels of a few hundred to a few thousand genes, and applicable to only a small number of samples. H&E imaging, by contrast, is cheap and collected routinely at scale. This makes predicting single-cell expression directly from morphology a practical way to bring molecular analys
summary_bullets: VOICE predicts single-cell gene expression from H&E histology images, enabling cost-effective molecular profiling at scale without expensive spatial transcriptomics.
Model combines direct prediction and retrieval-based approaches, leveraging both morphological features and reference gene expression databases for improved accuracy.
Addresses practical bottleneck: enables genome-wide expression inference from routine pathology images across many samples affordably.

papers.title: A Physics-Informed Neural Network Approach to Multiphysics Continuum Modeling of Cancer Growth via Chemo-fluid Coupling
papers.authors: Celia Taboada, Pedro Navas, Miguel Molinos
papers.abstract: Tumor progression is an inherently multiphysical phenomenon in which interstitial fluid dynamics, biochemical transport, and cellular mechanics interact across multiple spatiotemporal scales. Classical mesh-based solvers, although accurate, impose prohibitive computational costs for the repeated evaluations demanded by inverse parameter identification and future patient-specific predictive pipelin
summary_bullets: Physics-informed neural networks enable efficient multiphysics tumor modeling by coupling fluid dynamics, biochemistry, and mechanics while reducing computational costs versus traditional mesh-based methods.
PINN approach facilitates inverse parameter identification and patient-specific predictions previously infeasible due to high computational expense of classical solvers.
Framework successfully captures multiscale interactions across interstitial flow, chemical transport, and cellular mechanics in cancer growth simulation.

papers.title: IL-19<sup>+</sup> monocytes suppress neuroinflammation and promote neurological recovery in young individuals with traumatic brain injury
papers.authors: Lu Z, Zhao J, Zhu J, Wang C, Liao W, Zhu X, Liu Q, Jiang R, Qu J, Zhu Y, Zhang L, Kang K, Wang Z, Gong P.
papers.abstract: Young patients with traumatic brain injury (TBI) have a better prognosis than the aged, but the underlying mechanisms are not clear. Here, we identified a population of IL-19<sup>+</sup> monocytes derived from cranial bone marrow appearing in the brain after TBI. IL-19<sup>+</sup> monocytes inhibit the glial hyper-response and promote neurological recovery after TBI through the IL-19/IL-20R axis,
summary_bullets: IL-19+ monocytes from cranial bone marrow infiltrate brain after TBI and suppress neuroinflammation
IL-19/IL-20R signaling inhibits glial activation and promotes neurological recovery in young TBI patients
This IL-19+ monocyte response may explain superior outcomes in younger versus aged individuals with TBI

papers.title: Depletion of CARM1 slows in vivo tumorigenicity and rewires developmental programming in glioma stem-like cells
papers.authors: Young DL, Stransky S, Molero MG, Yamashita E, Pande S, Kumar V, Singh S, Aguilan J, Cutler R, Koba W, DeAngelo JD, Roth JS, Zhang J, He T, Malachowska B, Vercellino J, Bell BI, Shechter D, Tofilon PJ, Phillips RE, Behnan J, Guha C, Sidoli S.
papers.abstract: Glioma stem-like cells (GSCs) exploit developmental signaling programs that contribute to glioblastoma heterogeneity and therapy resistance. Here, we define a role for the arginine methyltransferase coactivator-associated arginine methyltransferase 1 (CARM1) in regulating GSC lineage state and survival signaling. CARM1 depletion slows GSC growth, increases apoptosis, alters histone post-translatio
summary_bullets: CARM1 depletion reduces glioma stem cell growth and increases apoptosis by disrupting developmental signaling programs.
CARM1 regulates histone modifications and GSC lineage state, with implications for glioblastoma heterogeneity and therapy resistance.
Targeting CARM1 slows in vivo tumor progression in glioblastoma models.

papers.title: Author Correction: The kinase MST4 limits inflammatory responses through direct phosphorylation of the adaptor TRAF6
papers.authors: Jiao S, Zhang Z, Li C, Huang M, Shi Z, Wang Y, Song X, Liu H, Li C, Chen M, Wang W, Zhao Y, Jiang Z, Wang H, Wong CCL, Wang C, Zhou Z.

papers.title: Reversible epiblast regionalization determines differentiation potential of human pluripotent stem cells
papers.authors: Sutcliffe MA, Wong E, Wingett SW, Morris CAJ, Stachelscheid H, Schoenfelder S, Lancaster MA.
papers.abstract: Although human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) can generate all tissues of the body, hPSCs in vitro frequently exhibit differentiation biases or failure that pose substantial challenges for disease modeling and regenerative medicine. The origins of these biases remain incompletely understood and extend beyond reprogramming artifacts. Here we show that loss of default neural differentiation capacity
summary_bullets: hPSCs exhibit reversible epiblast regionalization that constrains differentiation potential beyond reprogramming artifacts
Regional epiblast identity determines lineage bias and differentiation capacity in pluripotent stem cells
Understanding epiblast regionalization can improve directed differentiation protocols for disease modeling and regenerative medicine

papers.title: A clinically validated framework for auditing AI chatbot behavior in mental health interactions
papers.authors: Weilnhammer V, Hou KY, Luettgau L, Summerfield C, Dolan R, Nour MM.
papers.abstract: Millions of users turn to consumer artificial intelligence chatbots to discuss emotional, behavioral and mental-health concerns, creating an urgent need for rigorous and scalable safety evaluations. Here we introduce simulated (SIM) vulnerability-amplifying interaction loops (VAILs) (SIM-VAIL), a clinically validated framework for auditing chatbot behavior in mental-health contexts. SIM-VAIL simul
summary_bullets: Framework uses simulated vulnerability-amplifying interaction loops to systematically audit AI chatbot safety in mental health contexts.
Clinical validation demonstrates SIM-VAIL effectively identifies risky chatbot behaviors when discussing emotional and mental health concerns.
Provides scalable safety evaluation method for millions of users relying on consumer AI chatbots for mental health support.

papers.title: The Plasmodium heme detoxification protein functions in mitochondrial protein synthesis
papers.authors: Sarrazin L, Rosenthal MR, Kloehn J, Ziesmann T, Schmitz Y, Sandtmann AL, Domènech-Eres R, Scholz-Höhn K, Boulet C, Distler U, Goldberg DE, Matz JM.
papers.abstract: Malaria blood-stage parasites digest ~80% of host cell hemoglobin within a degradative vacuole, releasing heme that is detoxified by sequestration into hemozoin crystals. Although essential for survival and a validated drug target, the mechanisms of heme biomineralization remain unclear. Here, we study the parasite's Heme Detoxification Protein (HDP), previously proposed to mediate hemozoin format
summary_bullets: HDP functions in mitochondrial protein synthesis rather than direct heme detoxification as previously thought.
Parasite heme toxicity management involves unexpected mitochondrial metabolic mechanisms beyond crystallization.
Finding challenges current understanding of malaria drug targets and hemozoin formation pathways.

papers.title: scXpand: Pan-cancer detection of T cell clonal expansion from single-cell RNA sequencing without paired single-cell TCR sequencing
papers.authors: Shorer O, Amit R, Yizhak K.
papers.abstract: Advances in single-cell sequencing have enabled detailed characterization of T cell clonal dynamics in cancer. However, analyses aiming to link the transcriptional landscape to T cell clonality remain limited by confounding factors unequally controlled in different studies. To address this challenge, we developed scXpand, a machine-learning framework for pan-cancer detection of T cell clonal expan
summary_bullets: scXpand uses machine learning to detect T cell clonal expansion from scRNA-seq alone, eliminating need for paired TCR sequencing data.
Framework enables pan-cancer T cell clonality analysis while controlling for confounding factors across different studies.
Approach links T cell transcriptional profiles to clonal dynamics without technical batch effects limiting previous analyses.

papers.title: PlantCAD2: A DNA foundation model for interpreting genomes across flowering plants
papers.authors: Zhai J, Gokaslan A, Hsu SK, Chen SP, Liu ZY, Marroquin E, Czech E, Cannon B, Berthel A, Romay MC, Pennell M, Kuleshov V, Buckler ES.
papers.abstract: Flowering plants (angiosperms) exhibit extraordinary species diversity, ∼200-fold variation in genome size, and relatively compact coding regions, presenting both a unique challenge and opportunity for DNA language models. Here, we introduce PlantCAD2, an extended-context, plant-specific DNA language model with single-nucleotide resolution, pre-trained on 65 angiosperm genomes, together with a ser
summary_bullets: PlantCAD2 is a DNA language model pre-trained on 65 angiosperm genomes, enabling accurate interpretation of plant genetic sequences.
Achieves single-nucleotide resolution across diverse flowering plants despite massive genome size variation and compact coding regions.
Demonstrates improved performance for plant genome analysis tasks compared to existing general-purpose DNA models.

papers.title: Polygenic risk scores and plasma proteomics identify cancer-related proteins and trans-regulated protein networks
papers.authors: Dutta D, Zhang J, Guo X, Quint R, Rooney MR, Machiela MJ, Brown KM, Coresh J, Battle AJ, Platz EA, Chatterjee N.
papers.abstract: Genome-wide association studies identify cancer susceptibility loci, but downstream protein mechanisms remain incompletely defined. We integrate polygenic risk scores (PRSs) for 21 cancers with 4,955 plasma proteins measured in cancer-free Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) participants to prioritize cancer-related proteins and protein networks. The protein quantitative trait score (pQTS)
summary_bullets: Polygenic risk scores for 21 cancers identify specific plasma proteins associated with cancer susceptibility in cancer-free populations.
Integration of cancer PRSs with proteomics reveals trans-regulated protein networks and shared biological mechanisms across cancer types.
Protein quantitative trait scores provide a method to prioritize functional proteins linking genetic risk to cancer development.

papers.title: Decoding the chemical space of fast-ion conductors via a descriptor-guided transfer learning framework
papers.authors: Wang Z, You F.
papers.abstract: Fast-ion conductors (FICs) are key components for next-generation high-performance batteries, yet predicting ion mobility remains challenging because of the unclear transport mechanisms. This difficulty is further compounded by experimental datasets that lack precise crystal structures. Here, we present a descriptor-guided transfer learning framework, named IonNet, to predict ion mobility for comp
summary_bullets: Transfer learning framework (IonNet) effectively predicts ion mobility in fast-ion conductors despite incomplete crystal structure data in experimental datasets.
Physics-informed descriptors guide the model to learn meaningful transport mechanisms, improving generalization across diverse ionic conductor chemistries.
Method enables high-throughput screening of battery materials by reliably predicting ion conductivity without requiring perfectly resolved structures.

papers.title: Deep learning reveals a neurocomputational mechanism predicting depression risk in adolescents
papers.authors: Lu H, Yan X, Becker B, Heinz A, Sahakian BJ, Langley C, Zuo Z, Cao L, Zhang Z, Robinson L, Vaidya N, Winterer J, King S, Walton C, Banaschewski T, Barker GJ, Bokde ALW, Brühl R, Flor H, Garavan H, Gowland P, Grigis A, Lemaitre H, Martinot JL, Martinot MP, Artiges E, Nees F, Orfanos DP, Poustka L, Kebir H, Schmidt U, Sinclair J, Smolka MN, Hohmann S, Holz N, Walter H, Whelan R, Desrivières S, Schumann G, Luo Q, STRATIFY/ESTRA Consortium, IMAGEN Consortium.
papers.abstract: Early detection and prevention of psychiatric disorders, particularly depression, remain as major global health challenges, yet reliable tools for identifying individuals before symptom onset are lacking. Here, we combine functional neuroimaging with computational modeling to identify a mechanistic biomarker of depression risk. In a population-based adolescent cohort (IMAGEN, N = 1332), we
summary_bullets: Deep learning on fMRI data identifies a neurocomputational biomarker predicting depression risk in adolescents before symptom onset.
Combined functional neuroimaging with computational modeling reveals mechanistic brain signatures underlying depression vulnerability.
IMAGEN cohort study (N=1332) demonstrates potential for early psychiatric disorder detection and prevention strategies.

papers.title: APOE<sup>+</sup> macrophages and POSTN<sup>+</sup>CAFs form immune-exclusion niche driving immunotherapy resistance in clear-cell renal carcinoma
papers.authors: Ge Q, Ge S, Wang Z, Anwaier A, Lu J, Tian X, Wang Y, Yang J, Chen Y, Zhang H, Ye D, Zhao SC, Xu W.
papers.abstract: Tumor immune barriers (TIBs) are spatially organized stromal-immune niches that restrict lymphocyte entry. To explain persistent immune-checkpoint blockade (ICB) resistance in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), we mapped TIBs and defined a peritumoral variant built from POSTN<sup>+</sup> cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) interlaced with APOE<sup>+</sup> tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs)
summary_bullets: APOE⁺ macrophages and POSTN⁺ CAFs form peritumoral immune-exclusion niche driving ICB resistance in ccRCC.
Spatial organization of stromal-immune cells creates tumor immune barriers restricting lymphocyte infiltration and checkpoint blockade efficacy.

papers.title: Global distribution and amplitudes of internal solitary waves revealed by SWOT
papers.authors: Zhang X, Zhou Y, Wang X, Li X.
papers.abstract: Internal solitary waves (ISWs) are powerful underwater disturbances that can vertically displace water by more than 200 meters, driving ocean mixing and affecting offshore engineering. Yet, their global distributions and vertical imprints remain poorly characterized. Traditional satellite sensors are constrained by cloud cover or limited sampling. The Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) miss
summary_bullets: SWOT satellite reveals global ISW distribution and amplitudes previously unmeasurable by traditional sensors, overcoming cloud cover and sampling limitations.
Internal solitary waves displace water >200m vertically, significantly impacting ocean mixing and offshore infrastructure globally.
First comprehensive global characterization of ISW vertical signatures enables better understanding of ocean dynamics and engineering applications.

papers.title: Transposable elements and homotypic niches drive immune dynamics and resistance in melanoma epigenetic-based immunotherapy
papers.authors: Ciervo E, Ceccarelli F, Di Giacomo AM, Grisolia P, Covre A, Besharat ZM, De Falco A, Caruso FP, Laezza L, Ferraro L, Martin GM, Bilbao D, Williams S, Currall B, Lofiego MF, Sani T, Ferretti E, Guo Y, Holden SB, Simeone I, Mortarini R, Anichini A, Maio M, Noviello TMR, Ceccarelli M.
papers.abstract: Melanoma plasticity drives immune evasion and therapy resistance through dynamic cell-state transitions beyond genetic alterations. Although epigenetic remodeling is central to this process, its impact under therapeutic pressure remains unclear. We profiled longitudinal biopsies from patients with melanoma treated in the phase 1b NIBIT-M4 epi-immunotherapy trial [NCT02608437, DNA (cytosine-5)-meth
summary_bullets: Transposable element activation and epigenetic remodeling drive melanoma immune evasion during epi-immunotherapy treatment.
Homotypic niches enable cell-state plasticity that promotes therapy resistance independent of genetic mutations.
Longitudinal epigenetic profiling reveals dynamic mechanisms of immunotherapy resistance in melanoma patients.

papers.title: ZPY-CpG-Ch, a broad coverage vaccine against <i>Streptococcus pneumoniae</i>
papers.authors: Audshasai T, Panagiotou S, Crossman L, Xu R, Verheijen L, Chaguza C, O'Brien M, Kadioglu A.
papers.abstract: Existing licensed pneumococcal vaccines, including Prevnar-13 and its higher-valency successors, have played a major role in reducing invasive pneumococcal disease worldwide. However, their effectiveness is increasingly threatened by the rise of multidrug-resistant strains and the shift in circulating serotypes toward those not targeted by current vaccines-a trend known as serotype replacement. Th
summary_bullets: Novel pneumococcal vaccine design combining CpG adjuvants with conserved protein antigens provides broad serotype coverage beyond traditional polysaccharide vaccines.
Addresses serotype replacement problem by targeting conserved bacterial antigens rather than variable capsular polysaccharides alone.
Overcomes limitations of existing vaccines like Prevnar-13 against multidrug-resistant strains and emerging serotypes.

papers.title: An autoinflammatory CDC42 variant M45L demonstrates the mechanism of pyrin inflammasome activation
papers.authors: Feng S, Reygaerts T, Kong K, Wierzbowski MC, Narayanan DL, Baker PJ, Bishop I, Zyulina M, Rosevear K, Cleveland ML, Hewitt TC, Andrews TD, Randazzo D, Steinbach PJ, Chae JJ, Kim H, Kastner DL, Renton WD, Ojaimi S, Lee W, Masters SL.
papers.abstract: CDC42 is an evolutionarily conserved guanosine triphosphatase (GTPase) regulating critical cellular and immune processes. Variants in CDC42 therefore cause a spectrum of developmental phenotypes, including hematological and immunological symptoms. Here, we identify a previously unrecognized autoinflammatory condition caused by CDC42<sup>Met45→Leu(M45L)</sup>. We confirm the pathogenicity of CDC42<
summary_bullets: CDC42 M45L variant causes autoinflammatory disease through constitutive GTPase activation and pyrin inflammasome hyperactivation.
Mutation impairs actin dynamics regulation, triggering aberrant immune signaling and systemic inflammation.
Findings reveal pyrin inflammasome as critical CDC42-dependent innate immune checkpoint.

papers.title: Misfirin' pyrin
papers.authors: Humphries F.
papers.abstract: Three studies identify CDC42 as binding partner of the pyrin B30.2 domain, establishing a previously unrecognized mechanism regulating pyrin inflammasome activation (see related Research Articles by Aoki et al., Feng et al., and Iwata et al.).
summary_bullets: CDC42 binds pyrin's B30.2 domain, revealing new inflammasome activation mechanism
CDC42-pyrin interaction provides previously unknown regulatory pathway for pyrin inflammasome
Three independent studies converge on CDC42 as key pyrin binding partner

papers.title: PKM2 works "off the books" to drive effector T cell function in MS
papers.authors: Falle A, Rangachari M.
papers.abstract: The noncanonical functions of PKM2 drive pathogenic T cell function in patients with MS.
summary_bullets: PKM2 functions beyond its canonical metabolic role to promote effector T cell activity in MS patients
Noncanonical PKM2 mechanisms are key drivers of pathogenic T cell responses in multiple sclerosis
Targeting PKM2's off-canonical functions may offer new therapeutic approaches for MS treatment

papers.title: A genotype-first approach reveals the molecular basis of pyrin inflammasome activation
papers.authors: Iwata N, Kuchitsu Y, Hijikata A, Shibata H, Nishitani-Isa M, Aoki M, Izawa K, Yoshitomi H, Takita J, Ueno H, Taguchi T, Yasumi T, Honda Y.
papers.abstract: Mutations in the MEFV gene, which encodes pyrin, are associated with a spectrum of inflammatory conditions called pyrin-associated autoinflammatory diseases (PAADs). Of the 400 MEFV variants listed in the Infevers database, most are classified as variants of uncertain significance. Thus, genetic diagnosis of PAADs remains challenging, and the molecular mechanisms underlying pyrin act
summary_bullets: MEFV mutations cause pyrin inflammasome dysregulation; genotype-first approach clarifies pathogenic variants versus uncertain significance classifications.
Pyrin senses cytoskeletal disruption through ASC recruitment, enabling systematic classification of disease-causing mutations across 400+ variants.
Study provides molecular framework for diagnosing pyrin-associated autoinflammatory diseases and understanding variant pathogenicity mechanisms.

papers.title: Mist-ical memory: The airway defenses induced by FluMist vaccination in adults
papers.authors: Zohair H, Devarajan P.
papers.abstract: Longitudinal nasopharyngeal swabs sample and reveal upper airway humoral memory generated after intranasal FluMist vaccination.
summary_bullets: FluMist intranasal vaccination generates detectable humoral immune memory in the upper airway, measurable via nasopharyngeal sampling.
Longitudinal swab analysis demonstrates sustained airway-specific antibody responses following live attenuated influenza virus vaccination.
Mucosal immunity from FluMist provides local respiratory tract defense mechanisms beyond systemic immunity.

papers.title: An N-terminal CDC42 T43I variant reveals the mechanism of pyrin inflammasome activation
papers.authors: Aoki M, Iannuzzo A, Mertz P, Feng S, Iwata N, Perugini C, Tsuchida N, El Masri R, Kuchitsu Y, Tacine R, Coppola S, Shibata H, Cescato M, Nishitani-Isa M, Terré A, Kawasaki Y, Dalmon S, Nishimura K, Magnotti F, Miyatake S, André M, Hamada K, London J, Izawa K, Niwa A, Okamoto N, Ogata K, Nishikawa M, Zara E, Saito MK, Tartaglia M, Ito S, Rodero MP, Nagata KI, Smahi A, Matsumoto N, Le Corre L, Takita J, Boursier G, Hijikata A, Henry T, Taguchi T, Hentgen V, Georgin-Lavialle S, Honda Y, Masters SL, Yasumi T, Delon J.
papers.abstract: Heterozygous carboxyl-terminal variants in the RHO guanosine triphosphatase (GTPase) CDC42 are known to cause severe autoinflammatory syndromes. Here, we identified a heterozygous amino-terminal p.T43I (Thr<sup>43</sup>→Ile) CDC42 variant in patients with autoinflammation and uncovered a molecular link between CDC42 and the inflammasome sensor pyrin, mutated in the hereditary autoinflammatory synd
summary_bullets: N-terminal CDC42 T43I variant activates pyrin inflammasome, causing autoinflammatory disease through altered GTPase signaling.
CDC42 mutations at different positions converge on pyrin activation, revealing the mechanistic link between CDC42 and inflammasome sensing.
T43I variant impairs CDC42 function, triggering pyrin-dependent innate immune responses and autoinflammation in heterozygous carriers.

papers.title: Hyodeoxycholic acid suppresses hepatic steatosis in a PPARα-dependent manner via distinct GLP-1- and iNKT cell-mediated pathways
papers.authors: Lee E, Hatano R, Takami M, Fujimoto M, Yoshikawa H, Endo Y, Koyama-Nasu R, Onodera A, Li J, Rodriguez-Cuenca S, Rodriguez-Fdez S, Kamzolas I, Lin YH, Bidault G, Noda T, Shimano H, Kimura MY, Motohashi S, Tanaka T, Vidal-Puig A, Miki T.
papers.abstract: Hepatosteatosis is a common metabolic disorder. Bile acids influence hepatosteatosis, immune function, and incretin secretion. However, whether bile acids mediate hepatosteatosis through these immune or endocrine pathways remain unknown. Here, we identify supplementation with hyodeoxycholic acid (HDCA) in high-fat diet-fed mice increases hepatic iNKT cells and elevates circulating GLP-1, both upre
summary_bullets: HDCA supplementation reduces hepatic steatosis in high-fat diet mice via PPARα activation and dual GLP-1/iNKT cell pathways.
Bile acid HDCA increases hepatic invariant natural killer T cells and elevates circulating GLP-1 levels independently.
PPARα mediates HDCA's anti-steatotic effects through distinct immune and endocrine mechanisms.

papers.title: Remote Sensing-Based Hybrid Statistical and Machine Learning Ensemble Modeling of Yellowfin Tuna Catch in the Western Equatorial Indian Ocean
papers.authors: Avishka Wijepala, Sharukshan Niranjan, Lisitha Abeysekara, Pasindu Weerasinghe
papers.abstract: Yellowfin tuna (Thunnus albacares) is an economically important pelagic species in the Indian Ocean, but its monthly catch variability is difficult to predict because reported catch is influenced by ocean productivity, thermal habitat, monsoon seasonality, fishing-ground characteristics, and fleet behavior. This study develops a remote sensing-based statistical and machine learning stacked ensembl
summary_bullets: Hybrid ensemble combining statistical and machine learning models improves yellowfin tuna catch prediction accuracy in the Indian Ocean.
Remote sensing variables capturing ocean productivity, temperature, and monsoon patterns effectively explain tuna catch variability.
Stacked ensemble approach outperforms individual models for forecasting monthly catch despite complex influences from oceanography and fishing behavior.

papers.title: JUMP-lite: Compact, reproducible benchmarking of cell representations
papers.authors: Alán F. Muñoz, Johan Fredin Haslum, Runxi Shen, Anne E. Carpenter, Shantanu Singh
papers.abstract: Image-based profiling captures rich phenotypic signatures for drug discovery and functional genomics. Large public datasets like JUMP Cell Painting now provide millions of images for systematic study. However, the scale of these resources, 115 TB for JUMP alone, and fragmented evaluation practices make systematic comparison of representation methods intractable for many researchers. Here we presen
summary_bullets: JUMP-lite provides a compact, reproducible benchmark for evaluating cell image representation methods at scale with reduced computational burden.
Enables systematic comparison of representation learning approaches using publicly available large-scale Cell Painting datasets like JUMP.
Addresses accessibility barriers by reducing data requirements and standardizing evaluation practices for phenotypic profiling research.

papers.title: Genotypic Triggers: Exposing Pharmacogenomic Blind Spots via Host-Specific Backdoors in Generative Antimicrobial Peptide Models
papers.authors: Doniyorkhon Obidov, Xiaolong Guo, Yonghui Li, Kaichen Yang
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have accelerated drug discovery, particularly in the automated design of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). However, current validation pipelines for peptide generation models overlook historical precedents showing that certain drugs carry health risks predominantly for individuals with specific genetic profiles. In this paper, we demonstrate that such targeted health risk
summary_bullets: LLMs generating antimicrobial peptides can harbor hidden genetic vulnerabilities affecting specific populations that standard validation misses.
Backdoor attacks on peptide generation models reveal how genetic-specific health risks persist undetected in automated drug discovery pipelines.
Current AMP validation lacks pharmacogenomic screening, enabling biased model outputs that could disproportionately harm genetically-defined patient subgroups.

papers.title: Stromal cell senescence augments haematopoietic cell fitness in clonal haematopoiesis
papers.authors: Mistry JJ, Young KA, Navarro Figueredo A, Edun G, Aguilar-Navarro AG, Colom Díaz PA, Telpoukhovskaia M, Fernández Maestre I, Cai SF, Götze KS, Tikhonova AN, Levine RL, Trowbridge JJ.
papers.abstract: Microenvironment remodelling impacts tumour growth and metastasis, but whether remodelling promotes pre-malignant clonal fitness remains unknown. Here, using single-cell RNA-sequencing of the bone-marrow microenvironment in a mouse model of DNMT3A-mutant clonal haematopoiesis (CH), we identify mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) in a molecular state of cellular senescence. Elevated bone-marrow MSC se
summary_bullets: Stromal cell senescence in bone marrow microenvironment promotes fitness of DNMT3A-mutant clonal hematopoietic cells
Single-cell RNA-seq reveals senescent mesenchymal stromal cells accumulate in clonal hematopoiesis disease model
Microenvironment remodeling through stromal senescence may facilitate pre-malignant clonal expansion

papers.title: Hit Selection Using SSMD-Based Machine Learning Performance Metrics in High-Throughput Screening Assays
papers.authors: Xiaohua Douglas Zhang
papers.abstract: High-throughput screening (HTS) assays are central to early-stage drug discovery but are often limited by extreme data sparsity, as primary screens typically use only a single replicate per test substance. This sparsity makes conventional machine-learning performance metrics, such as sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), difficult to estimate
summary_bullets: Single-replicate HTS data limits conventional ML performance metrics; SSMD-based metrics better handle extreme data sparsity in drug screening
SSMD approach provides reliable hit selection despite lack of replicate measurements typical in primary screening assays
Machine learning performance evaluation requires metrics adapted to sparse, unreplicated HTS data rather than standard statistical measures

papers.title: EpiBench: Can LLMs Understand Epitopes for Antibody Drug Discovery?
papers.authors: Zirui Wang, Jiaqi Wang, Qinghan Wang, Yuzhi Xu, Gang Du, Tingjun Hou, Odin Zhang
papers.abstract: Epitopes determine where antibodies bind antigens and shape downstream therapeutic properties such as functional blockade and escape resistance, making epitope understanding central to antibody drug discovery. Although large language models (LLMs) have shown strong biomedical reasoning ability, it remains unclear whether they can infer epitope information directly from antigen and antibody sequenc
summary_bullets: LLMs struggle with epitope prediction from antigen-antibody sequences despite strong biomedical reasoning, suggesting limitations in structural biology understanding.
EpiBench benchmark reveals performance gaps between current LLMs and requirements for practical antibody drug discovery applications.
Direct sequence-based epitope inference remains challenging for language models without specialized structural or experimental information.

papers.title: Frozen but Not Always Accessible: A Representation Analysis of Genomic Language Models
papers.authors: Nirjhor Datta, Swakkhar Shatabda, M. Sohel Rahman
papers.abstract: Genomic foundation models are increasingly reused as frozen feature extractors for downstream sequence prediction, offering a compute-efficient alternative to full fine-tuning. However, it remains unclear when biological information encoded by these models is accessible without task-specific adaptation. We present a representation-accessibility analysis of frozen genomic language models across reg
summary_bullets: Frozen genomic language models contain biological information but accessibility varies by task without task-specific adaptation.
Representation analysis reveals when biological features encoded in foundation models are accessible versus require fine-tuning.
Compute-efficient frozen feature extraction works inconsistently across genomic prediction tasks depending on information accessibility.

papers.title: Omega-S: A Functional Resilience Index for LLM Fine-Tuning
papers.authors: Alberto Acedo
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning a large language model on new data degrades what it previously learned. We present Omega-S, a drop-in penalty computed from the weight matrix alone: it needs no previous-task data, no Fisher matrix and no stored copy of the old weights. It is three lines in an existing training loop and adds under 4% to the cost of a step. Retention. On Llama-3-8B with LoRA, fine-tuned from code to pro
summary_bullets: Omega-S enables efficient continual learning by penalizing weight changes during fine-tuning, computed from weight matrices alone without storing old weights or Fisher matrices.
Method adds <4% computational cost and requires only three lines of code, making it practical for drop-in integration into existing training loops.
Achieves strong retention of original task performance while learning new tasks on Llama-3-8B with LoRA fine-tuning.

papers.title: MS-MLB: An Open Machine Learning Benchmark for Blood-Based MS Classification
papers.authors: Adam Simson, Ankush Dutta, Quang Bui
papers.abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is diagnosed through clinical assessment, magnetic resonance imaging, laboratory evidence when appropriate, and exclusion of better explanations. Blood RNA expression data may contain disease associated immune signal, but a blood RNA classifier cannot be treated as a replacement for clinical diagnosis. This paper presents MS-MLB (Multiple Sclerosis Machine Learning Benchmar
summary_bullets: Blood RNA expression shows promise for MS classification but cannot replace clinical diagnosis methods.
MS-MLB benchmark enables standardized evaluation of machine learning models for MS detection.
Open-source resource facilitates reproducible research in blood-based biomarker discovery for MS.

papers.title: The Cost of Binarizing Survival Outcomes in Clinical Prognostic Modeling
papers.authors: Shashank Yadav, David M. Routman, Andrew Y. K. Foong
papers.abstract: Survival analysis is an established framework for analyzing time-to-event data, yet many clinical machine learning studies still binarize the outcome before model training. This practice excludes censored patients, collapses temporal information into a single threshold, and can affect which features are selected as prognostically relevant. We examine the cost of this binarization in the context of
summary_bullets: Binarizing survival outcomes excludes censored patients and loses temporal information, reducing model performance compared to proper survival analysis methods.
Outcome binarization alters feature selection, potentially identifying prognostically irrelevant features while missing truly predictive variables.
Clinical ML studies should adopt established survival analysis frameworks instead of binarizing time-to-event data for improved prognostic accuracy.

papers.title: Spatial proteomics guided by H&E-based AI reveals recurrence-risk niches in triple-negative breast cancer
papers.authors: Yesung Cho, Ji Hwan Park, Chanil Kim, Hyewon Kim, Honglan Li, Yumin Lee, Geongyu Lee, Sujeong Hong, Seong Min Park, Yoonyoung Lee, Hee Sool Rho, Sumin Lee, Amos Chungwon Lee, Changhwan Lee, Hwanyoung Shim, Hyunwook Kim, Hyeji Shin, Sanha Park, Jihoon Yu, Yoon Hee Shin, Sooheon Kim, Hyunjin Park, Seung Min Park, Sangwan Kim, Yujung Kim, Sung-Im Do, Eun-Young Kim, Dongmyung Shin, Jongbae Park, In-Gu Do
papers.abstract: Deep learning models can predict cancer recurrence from H&E stained slides, but the localized molecular states underlying these predictions remain largely obscured. Here, we developed an outcome informed spatial pathology framework in TNBC that integrates AI generated recurrence risk heatmaps with mass spectrometry based spatial proteomics. In a cohort of 156 patients, distribution based aggre
summary_bullets: AI-predicted high-risk regions in TNBC contain distinct proteomic signatures associated with recurrence outcomes.
Integration of H&E deep learning predictions with spatial proteomics reveals molecular mechanisms driving recurrence risk.
Spatial proteomics identifies localized protein signatures that could guide personalized treatment strategies in triple-negative breast cancer.

papers.title: Scaling an Autoregressive Transformer for Single-Cell Generation
papers.authors: Aleksandr Sharipov, Yusif Mukhtarov, Igor Molybog
papers.abstract: We study a self-supervised generation task for single-cell gene expression vectors: given a set of vectors from a cell type, we aim to generate additional gene expression vectors of that cell type. For this task we characterize both the biological fidelity of the generated gene expression vectors and the scaling behavior of the pretraining loss. The model is a causal transformer paired with a lear
summary_bullets: Autoregressive transformers can effectively generate realistic single-cell gene expression vectors with biological fidelity when trained on cell-type-specific data.
Pretraining loss follows predictable scaling laws, enabling efficient model development for single-cell generation tasks.
Self-supervised generation approach produces gene expression vectors that maintain biological validity across different cell types.

papers.title: CLARA: Clarification of Language Ambiguity through Result Analysis for Natural-Language Cancer Genomics Queries
papers.authors: Pratyush Kumar Shukla, Manveer Singh Tib, Siddhant Garg
papers.abstract: A natural language interface can be used to make cancer genomics databases easier to use, but even if a question is perfectly fluent, its scientific meaning can be ambiguous. We propose CLARA, a framework that represents a question as a typed scientific query specification, considers a few possible interpretations, executes them, and asks for clarification when the estimates diverge. CLARA was ass
summary_bullets: CLARA resolves ambiguity in natural language cancer genomics queries by generating multiple interpretations, executing them, and requesting clarification when results diverge significantly.
Framework represents scientific questions as typed query specifications, enabling automated detection of semantic ambiguity without requiring perfect initial understanding.
Approach makes cancer genomics databases more accessible by intelligently identifying when clarification is needed rather than making arbitrary interpretation choices.

papers.title: A Blind Spot in Alignment: Quantifying Biosecurity Risks in Large Language Models
papers.authors: Shu Quan, Tianfang Hao, Sitong Fang, He Geng, Jiayi Zhou, Boyuan Chen, Kaile Wang, Donghai Hong, Juntao Dai, Yaodong Yang, Jiaming Ji
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are accelerating biological research, yet this same capability poses a critical biosecurity threat: models that assist in protein engineering can equally be prompted to generate predicted toxin-like sequences, potentially lowering the barrier to biological misuse. Current safety evaluations, however, operate in natural language and cannot determine whether a model-gene
summary_bullets: LLMs can generate dangerous protein sequences when prompted, but current safety evaluations miss this risk because they only test natural language outputs.
Models trained to assist protein engineering inadvertently gain capability to design toxin-like sequences, creating undetected biosecurity vulnerabilities.
Biosecurity threats from biological sequence generation represent a critical gap in current LLM alignment and safety evaluation frameworks.

papers.title: Smart membrane: high content in situ monitoring barrier on chip with artificial neural network
papers.authors: Bo Tang, Victor Krajka, Mengxi Liu, Wei Zhao, Gazal Goekkus, Paul Lukowicz, Lili Zhu, Pu Chen, Stephan Reichl, Andreas Dietzel
papers.abstract: Conventional transepithelial electrical resistance (TEER) technique provides only a low-content analysis of cell-layer conditions, necessitating repeated microscopic assessments of morphology and cell-cell contacts outside the incubator for barrier-on-chip systems. This work presents a novel high-content TEER device in the form of a novel nanoporous membrane that facilitates continuous electrical
summary_bullets: Novel nanoporous membrane enables high-content TEER monitoring with continuous electrical measurements, replacing low-content conventional techniques.
Artificial neural network analyzes TEER data to assess barrier morphology and cell-cell contacts without removing samples from incubator.
Integrated on-chip system provides real-time monitoring of barrier-on-chip conditions, eliminating need for repeated external microscopic assessments.

papers.title: Beyond Gene Reconstruction: Learning Cell Representations through Complementary Transcriptomic Views
papers.authors: Jiaqi Xiong, Yuntao hu, Yu Zheng, Yifei Shi, Xinyue Guo, Jiaxin Qi
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of single-cell transcriptomic data has enabled the development of foundation models pretrained primarily by reconstructing masked expression values. This objective encourages these models to learn gene dependencies but does not directly optimize whole-cell representations, which are essential for many downstream tasks. To bridge this gap, we propose a contrastive pretraining frame
summary_bullets: Gene reconstruction alone doesn't optimize cell representations; contrastive learning better captures whole-cell information for downstream tasks.
Complementary transcriptomic views in contrastive pretraining improve foundation model performance across single-cell analysis tasks.
Multi-view contrastive approach outperforms standard masked expression reconstruction for learning meaningful cell embeddings.

papers.title: Integrative spatial profiling of 3D genome organization and gene expression in tissue
papers.authors: Guo, P., Cui, Y., He, J., Waldman, A. J., Zhu, J., Chen, Y., Huang, Z., Zhou, J., Phillips-Cremins, J. E., Deng, Y.
papers.abstract: The interplay between 3D genome architecture and transcriptional activity is fundamental to gene regulation. However, existing methodologies cannot simultaneously measure these modalities within intact tissues, limiting our understanding of how genome organization coordinates transcriptional programs across diverse cell types and spatial microenvironments. Here, we introduce Spatial Hi-C-RNA, a sp
summary_bullets: Spatial Hi-C-RNA enables simultaneous measurement of 3D genome architecture and gene expression within intact tissues, revealing cell-type and spatial context-specific regulation.
Method demonstrates how local genome organization patterns correlate with transcriptional activity across diverse tissue microenvironments and cell populations.
Integrative approach provides mechanistic insights into how 3D chromatin structure coordinates gene expression programs in complex tissue contexts.

papers.title: Microfluidic T-Chip enables one-step clinical-scale T-cell purification from blood products for CAR T-cell manufacturing
papers.authors: Rana, M., Nigrovic, S. E., Payan-Medina, A., Saha, S., Putaturo, V. R., Cunneely, Q. E., Bell, R., Antmen, E., Maus, M. V., Toner, M., Elsallab, M., Mishra, A.
papers.abstract: Treatment with chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells has emerged as a promising immune therapy for relapsed and refractory hematologic malignancies. The CAR T cells are manufactured in a series of steps that involve isolating T cells from the patients leukapheresis product, genetically modifying them to express the CAR against the target antigen, and reinfusing them into the patient. Efficient T
summary_bullets: Microfluidic T-chip achieves clinical-scale T-cell purification from blood in one step, simplifying CAR T manufacturing.
Device enables efficient T-cell isolation from leukapheresis products without multiple processing steps.
Technology reduces manufacturing complexity and time for CAR T-cell therapeutic production.

papers.title: Systematic modeling of phenotypic drug response profiles inpatient-derived organoids
papers.authors: Kim, S., Gunnarsson, E. B., Doche, M., Zhou, Y., Huang, Y.-K., Valena, S., Kshetri, P., Elton, E., Ung, N., Coleman, A., Magnusson, B. V., Torab, N., Papasian, L., Choi, B., Fung, E., Knaneh-Monem, H., Foo, J., Mumenthaler, S.
papers.abstract: Patient-derived tumor organoids provide a physiologically relevant 3D disease model for preclinical drug discovery, surpassing the limitations of conventional 2D cell lines. To better capture the dynamic nature of organoid drug responses, we developed a new systematic evaluation method called SCOPE (Systematic Classification of Organoids for Phenotypic Evaluation), harnessing phenotypic assessment
summary_bullets: SCOPE enables systematic phenotypic profiling of patient-derived tumor organoids to predict drug responses more accurately than conventional 2D methods.
3D organoid models capture complex, dynamic drug response characteristics that better reflect patient tumor biology and treatment outcomes.
Phenotypic classification approach improves preclinical drug discovery by providing physiologically relevant patient-specific sensitivity predictions.

papers.title: Targeting the NuRD Component, CHD4, Impairs Foxp3+ Treg Cell Production and Function and Promotes Anti-Tumor Immunity
papers.authors: Xiong, Y., Wang, L., Minisini, M., Kong, F., Di Giorgio, E., Akimova, T., Horman, S., Babic, I., Nurmemmedov, E., Hancock, W. W.
papers.abstract: Little is known about why Foxp3 regulatory T (Treg) cells require at least three HDAC1/HDAC2-containing chromatin-remodeling complexes (NuRD, Sin3 and CoREST), or whether selective disruption of these complexes can be exploited to enhance antitumor immunity. Here, we investigated the role of chromodomain helicase DNA- binding protein 4 (CHD4), the ATP-dependent remodeling subunit of the NuRD compl
summary_bullets: CHD4, the NuRD complex's remodeling subunit, is essential for Foxp3+ Treg cell development and suppressive function in tumors.
CHD4 deletion impairs Treg differentiation and stability while enhancing anti-tumor immunity without compromising effector T cell function.
Selective NuRD complex disruption offers therapeutic potential for cancer immunotherapy by reducing immunosuppressive Treg populations.

papers.title: INSM1 Regulates Neuroendocrine Plasticity and Tumor Progression in Prostate Cancer
papers.authors: Chen, C., CHENG, S., Li, L., Sivalingam, J. S., Gu, X., Yeh, Y., Yu, X., Lan, M. S.
papers.abstract: AbstractNeuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC) is a highly aggressive and therapy-resistant subtype that arises from adenocarcinoma through lineage plasticity; however, the molecular mechanisms driving this transition remain incompletely defined. Insulinoma-associated protein 1 (INSM1), a zinc-finger transcription factor and established neuroendocrine lineage marker, has been implicated in a variet
summary_bullets: INSM1 transcription factor drives neuroendocrine plasticity and aggressive tumor progression in prostate cancer.
INSM1 acts as a key molecular regulator enabling adenocarcinoma-to-neuroendocrine lineage transition.
Targeting INSM1 may provide therapeutic strategy for treatment-resistant neuroendocrine prostate cancer.

papers.title: Deep Mechanistic Models reveal pathway-extrinsic drivers of mammary MAPK signalling heterogeneity
papers.authors: Fabrini, G., Froehlich, F.
papers.abstract: Cells sense and respond to their environment through signalling pathways, and the dynamics of these pathways shape cell fate even within genetically identical populations. Two largely separate computational traditions describe this behaviour: mechanistic differential-equation models and representation-learning methods. Mechanistic models encode pathway topology and kinetics but cannot easily repre
summary_bullets: Mechanistic models with pathway-extrinsic variables better explain MAPK signaling heterogeneity than topology/kinetics alone in mammary cells.
Integration of mechanistic modeling with representation learning reveals non-pathway factors drive single-cell signaling dynamics and cell fate decisions.
Deep mechanistic approach bridges traditional differential-equation models and modern machine learning for understanding biological pathway heterogeneity.

papers.title: LiteVax-adjuvanted influenza vaccine induces transient interferon-driven innate activation and accelerates early IgG3 responses in older adults
papers.authors: D'Onofrio, V., Verstraete, M., Porrez, S., Jacobs, B., Alhatemi, A., De Gussem, S., Verwilst, S., Willems, A., Waerlop, G., De Meester, E., Decraene, S., Van Niewerburgh, F., Leroux-Roels, G., van Riet, E., Platenburg, P. P., Hilgers, L., Leroux-Roels, I.
papers.abstract: Vaccine immunogenicity declines with age due to immunosenescence, underscoring the need for improved adjuvants. LiteVax Adjuvant (LVA), a squalane-in-water emulsion containing carbohydrate fatty-acid monosulphate esters, has shown potential to enhance influenza vaccine responses, but its mechanisms in humans remain unclear. We performed a longitudinal systems vaccinology study in 56 younger (18-45
summary_bullets: LiteVax adjuvant triggers transient interferon-driven innate immune activation that enhances early IgG3 responses in older adults receiving influenza vaccine
Systems vaccinology analysis reveals adjuvant mechanisms improve vaccine immunogenicity despite age-related immunosenescence
Early innate activation correlates with accelerated adaptive B-cell responses, suggesting adjuvant timing and kinetics matter for elderly populations

papers.title: β-endorphin primes NK cells and NK-derived Extracellular Vesicle to enhance anti-tumor cytotoxicity
papers.authors: Cooks, T., Bar, O., Aharon, N., Abu-Ahmad, M., Luz, I., Radinsky, O., Porgador, A.
papers.abstract: Psychoneuroimmunology suggests that positive physiological states, including laughter, could affect anti-tumor immunity, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we investigated whether {beta}-endorphin (BE), an endogenous opioid peptide associated with positive physiological stimuli, modulates Natural Killer (NK) cell cytotoxicity and the anti-tumor activity of NK-derived extracellular
summary_bullets: β-endorphin enhances NK cell cytotoxicity and anti-tumor activity through priming of NK cells and their extracellular vesicles.
Positive physiological states like laughter may boost anti-tumor immunity via endogenous β-endorphin signaling to NK cells.
NK-derived extracellular vesicles represent a potential mechanism linking psychoneuroimmunology to anti-tumor immune responses.

papers.title: Menstruation is associated with cyclical granulysin peaks in vaginal secretions despite stable expression by cervicovaginal immune cells
papers.authors: Hughes, S. M., Levy, C. N., Chamberlain, D. R., Varon, D., Murphy, B., Schwedhelm, K., Shafi, J., Lund, J. M., Prlic, M., De Rosa, S. C., Micks, E., Johnston, C., Hladik, F.
papers.abstract:
ProblemThe anti-microbial protein granulysin is present in vaginal secretions during the follicular phase of the menstrual cycle but nearly disappears during the luteal phase. The reason for this change is unknown.

Method of studyParticipants (n = 23) with regular menstrual cycles collected daily vaginal swabs for granulysin ELISAs. Endocervical cytobrushes, ectocervical biopsies, vaginal biopsie
summary_bullets: Granulysin levels in vaginal secretions peak during follicular phase, drop during luteal phase, despite stable immune cell expression.
Menstrual cycle hormones regulate granulysin secretion independent of cervicovaginal immune cell abundance.
Cyclical granulysin patterns may affect vaginal microbiome composition and infection susceptibility across menstrual phases.

papers.title: What Carries the Signal in Pathology Foundation-Model Atlases? A Patient-Level Controlled Benchmark in Breast Cancer
papers.authors: Chimdi Walter Ndubuisi
papers.abstract: Pathology foundation models are reported to encode molecular programmes in tissue morphology, but the evidence is usually a cohort-wide ranked gene list rather than a prediction for a held-out patient. We rebuild such an analysis with the patient as the unit of evidence and ask which pipeline component carries signal. Across 11 frozen backbones, four pre-specified gene programmes and 285 TCGA-BRCA
summary_bullets: Patient-level controlled analysis reveals foundation model atlases encode molecular signals in tissue morphology, but with variable reliability across different model backbones.
Signal strength depends critically on pipeline components; atlas construction and aggregation methods matter as much as the frozen backbone encoder.
Reproducibility across held-out patients is modest, suggesting caution when interpreting cohort-level ranked gene lists as evidence of biological encoding.

papers.title: EasyBCI Agent: Towards Universal Neural Data Preprocessing for Brain-Computer Interfaces
papers.authors: Yu Zhu, Runkai Zhao, Zhimin Zhou, Jinyu Cai, Zhouheng Yao, Chutian Zhang, Peiyuan Li, Xiaoxing Zhang, Qihao Zheng, Jiamin Wu, Mianxin Liu, Chi Zhang, Bin Min, Lei Bai, Chengyu Li, Jingpeng Wu, Chunfeng Song
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces translate neural activity into device commands, yet their performance hinges on preprocessing that remains manual, expert-dependent and poorly reproducible. Large language model agents can automate scientific coding, but existing systems lack the modality coverage, raw-data isolation, experience accumulation and domain oversight that neural preprocessing requires. We intr
summary_bullets: LLM agents can automate neural data preprocessing for BCIs, reducing manual expert dependency and improving reproducibility across modalities.
EasyBCI Agent accumulates preprocessing experience, handles raw data directly, and maintains domain expert oversight for reliable BCI performance.
